method: Read the33page main-body text; inspect all33rendered pages in six contact sheets for page layout and figure context.
Compare stated objectives with named active Japanese paragraphs; distinguish an explanation from a merely related candidate.
Retain stable authored expression; restore four distinct paragraphs removed by overbroad deduplication.
Do not claim full-resolution label/table-cell recognition, complete atomic decomposition, or technical approval from contact sheets.
Record model/design/SDS/current-law requirements instead of universalizing numerical or operational source examples.

rows.objective: Distinguish an asphalt-emulsion distributor from a hand-guided compaction roller.
rows.remaining: Paving roles are taught generally, but these two named equipment identities and their visual distinctions need new bounded teaching/recognition checks.

rows.objective: Identify earth-drill bucket excavation and casing-based full-rotation excavation as different equipment arrangements.
rows.remaining: The cast-in-place pile concept is taught; bucket, casing and hammer-grab identities are not established by that general paragraph.

rows.objective: Relate the hammer grab to removing soil inside casing rather than to driving a finished pile.
rows.remaining: Author the component distinction and verify the picture labels; do not turn the source sketch into operating instructions.

rows.objective: Separate the purpose of pile-driving equipment from the excavating bucket/casing system.
rows.remaining: Material and construction-location distinctions exist; named equipment recognition remains to be taught.

rows.objective: Distinguish frame, wedge-fastened and tube-and-coupler scaffold systems by their component connections.
rows.remaining: A scaffold purpose and clamps/wall ties are taught; the three system identities need reviewed illustrations and explicit explanation.

rows.objective: Treat the source tube diameter as a specification for the depicted system, not a universal size or strength ranking.
rows.remaining: Verify the intended standard/product and comparison before teaching a numerical diameter or relative safety/strength claim.

rows.objective: Distinguish the working platform from bracing between uprights.
rows.remaining: Original paragraph restored at active revision2 with12translations. Named posts, base jacks, joints and brackets still require their own recognition mapping.

rows.objective: Identify sole support/base fittings, uprights and horizontal members without treating a part list as an approved assembly.
rows.remaining: The complete named component chain and diagram labels are not explained by the general candidates. Foundation, fastening and assembly decisions require the applicable system/design.

rows.objective: Separate tube joints, clamps, platform hooks and cantilever brackets by what they connect or support.
rows.remaining: Clamp function exists. Other named connector/support functions and compatibility conditions need teaching and verified recognition assets.

rows.objective: Separate toe-board, wall-tie and sound-containment functions.
rows.remaining: Wall ties and wind effects of sheeting are taught. Toe-board and product-specific sound/fire/weather performance need explicit bounded treatment.

rows.objective: Identify a retracting fall-arrest device and distinguish its function from a lifting block.
rows.remaining: Do not infer anchorage compatibility, usable direction, connection method or clearance from the photograph; obtain the device instructions and professional review.

rows.objective: Separate annealed tying wire from a claim that annealing universally increases its strength.
rows.remaining: The source strength wording needs materials/manufacturer verification. Do not copy it into a general rule.

rows.objective: Distinguish wire cutters, a shino tying tool and a shino-equipped ratchet wrench.
rows.remaining: Ratchet mechanism restored, but these specific tool identities and pictured ends are not all taught. Source wrench dimensions are examples, not procurement or loading rules.

rows.objective: Explain how a ratchet transmits rotation during a back-and-forth handle movement.
rows.remaining: Original paragraph restored with12translations; KTC primary explanation checked2026-10-17. This does not establish torque, capacity or a usage procedure.

rows.objective: Separate hole alignment from turning a fastener; identify the drift pin used in the source.
rows.remaining: The purpose distinction exists, but named drift-pin recognition and appropriate use conditions are not established.

rows.objective: Read open-end, ring/combination and impact-wrench features without treating every wrench as six-point and every spanner as two-point.
rows.remaining: Existing general terminology is bounded. Verify the exact pictured tools; source contact-point and offset-angle examples must not become universal classifications.

rows.objective: Separate cutting, bending and tying jobs in rebar equipment.
rows.remaining: The functional distinction is explicit. Hydraulic/manual/cordless model recognition and permissible materials/capacity remain separate product checks.

rows.objective: Separate wheel spacers, bar supports and mortar blocks by the rebar position they help retain.
rows.remaining: Cover and spacer purpose exist; the three pictured forms, their placement examples and compatibility need additional source-bound teaching.

rows.objective: Distinguish an exposed-end cap from a spacer supporting rebar position.
rows.remaining: Do not infer impact/impalement protection or load capacity from an unqualified plastic-cap photograph; obtain product-specific evidence.

rows.objective: Distinguish folding-ruler measurement, tying-wire material and a tying hook.
rows.remaining: General measuring and tying-tool roles exist. Exact folding-ruler form and tying-wire gauge are source examples needing scoped specification checks.

rows.objective: Retain identification linking the rebar shape, quantity and use location.
rows.remaining: Processing labels are explicitly explained; no need to duplicate the Japanese lesson or translations.

rows.objective: Separate holding the bars, applying axial pressure and heating the joint.
rows.remaining: Original paragraph restored with12translations. Pump, ram, hose and burner names/recognition are still more specific than this role explanation.

rows.objective: Trace pressure generation, transmission and actuation across pump, hose and ram-cylinder components.
rows.remaining: Requires bounded component descriptions and reviewed labels; this is not permission to give pressure, connection or startup instructions.

rows.objective: Distinguish heating burner, gas-mixing torch and the source valve/control accessory.
rows.remaining: Identify the exact device/model before teaching switching, ignition or gas handling. Do not generalize source automatic-control behavior to other systems.

rows.objective: Separate exterior dimensional inspection, ultrasonic examination, tensile testing and bend testing.
rows.remaining: The different information and distinction between test execution and approval are explained. No numerical acceptance criteria approved.

rows.objective: Understand the pictured pressure-welding auxiliary ring without generalizing its applicability.
rows.remaining: Check the particular approved method and component instructions before teaching ring performance, placement or reduced heating effects.

rows.objective: Separate the welding power source, base metal and consumable electrode.
rows.remaining: Original paragraph restored with12translations; JWES primary description checked. No electrical connection, current or welding-operation instruction introduced.

rows.objective: Explain the complementary compression/tension roles of concrete and reinforcing steel rather than a generic stronger-material claim.
rows.remaining: The active paragraph describes force resistance generally; verify that the intended compression/tension distinction is explicitly taught before marking the source objective covered.

rows.objective: Relate concrete alkalinity, carbonation and reinforcement corrosion with the relevant limits.
rows.remaining: Cover measurement exists, but it does not teach the corrosion mechanism. Needs verified conceptual teaching, not an invented universal carbonation rate.

rows.objective: Separate specified cover, bar diameter/pitch and overlap/bond requirements.
rows.remaining: The core geometry and bond concepts are explained. Any required dimensions, locations and inspection criteria must come from the applicable design/specification.

rows.objective: Coordinate embedded services, reinforcing steel, formwork and concrete before concealment.
rows.remaining: These interfaces are already explained; reuse the canonical teaching rather than repeating a second course.

rows.objective: Separate material identity, prepared end faces, holding/alignment and heating/pressure work.
rows.remaining: The joining principle and equipment roles are taught; process preparation and execution details require the applicable qualified method.

rows.objective: Do not teach one source heating span or stopping condition as universally applicable.
rows.remaining: Obtain current approved procedure and applicability before any dimensions, pressure, temperature, timing or completion criteria are taught.

rows.objective: Separate swelling geometry, axial misalignment, bending and cracking observations from acceptance.
rows.remaining: Inspection purposes exist. Specific defect names, figure labels and the relationship to acceptance criteria remain to be reconciled.

rows.objective: Separate current/arc conditions and visible weld appearance from proof of soundness.
rows.remaining: General variability and appearance limits exist. Do not supply welding settings or conclude quality from bead appearance.

rows.objective: Differentiate fumes, optical radiation and grinding dust as hazards needing task-specific controls.
rows.remaining: Hazards and protection-purpose distinctions are taught. Actual exposure controls, respiratory selection and grinding operations still require current task-specific professional review.

rows.objective: Trace fresh-concrete side pressure and construction loads through formwork and its support system.
rows.remaining: Core forces/components are explained. Assembly order, spacing, capacity and removal remain design/procedure-dependent.

rows.objective: Relate roofing layers, junction flashing, underlay and rainwater paths.
rows.remaining: General layers and repair limits exist; the specific junction/underlay/flashing relationship and labels need an explicit source-bound explanation.

rows.objective: Distinguish snow retention, wind resistance and the purposes of roof coating or plaster repair.
rows.remaining: Coating and fragile-roof hazards are taught. Snow-device role and applicable roof/regional conditions are not established; no universal waterproof promise.

rows.objective: Coordinate interior framing, services and board attachment before closure.
rows.remaining: Framework and board purpose exist; location/count/spacing and installation details need the specified system and coordination plan.

rows.objective: Do not generalize cutting paper, snapping or wet bending to every board/system.
rows.remaining: Check the actual board, thickness, radius and approved installation method; source instructions are insufficient for a universal operation.

rows.objective: Relate board joints and uneven substrate to tape, filling and finishing preparation.
rows.remaining: Joint filling and unevenness are explained. Tape/sanding system and task-specific dust controls require product/process evidence.

rows.objective: Keep sash material, airtightness, watertightness and installation interfaces separate.
rows.remaining: Existing teaching correctly allows resin/composite frames; do not replace it with the source universal aluminium/glass description.

rows.objective: Separate temporary positioning, alignment, designed anchors, perimeter closure and final operation checks.
rows.remaining: The welding-anchor and mortar detail in the source is one installation example. Confirm the frame/wall system and approved detail before teaching an operation.

rows.objective: Distinguish two-component liquid materials from the formed insulation layer and recognize substrate/coverage checks.
rows.remaining: Core material and adhesion/continuity concepts exist. This does not verify product handling or required thickness.

rows.objective: Treat storage temperature, shelf life and container pressure/reactivity as product-dependent conditions.
rows.remaining: Need the actual product SDS and handling instructions. Source storage values, direct-heat restrictions and contaminated/pressurized-container opening instructions are not adopted as universal procedures.

rows.objective: Separate proportioning, reaction/foam condition, substrate state and thickness inspection.
rows.remaining: No universal mix ratio, field adjustment, spray distance, temperature or test spacing approved; use specified equipment/product/process and qualified review.

rows.objective: Separate partial structural removal, site/utility isolation and adjacent public effects.
rows.remaining: Scope and neighbor effects exist. Isolation responsibilities and verification need current site-specific arrangements; an absence of use is not proof of disconnection.

rows.objective: Keep hazardous-material investigation and waste separation distinct.
rows.remaining: Canonical teaching already explains investigation and separation. Do not infer legal applicability/reporting requirements solely from the historical source area threshold.

rows.objective: Scope the source area-triggered recycling-law statement to current law and work category.
rows.remaining: No present-day threshold or filing duty approved by this audit; verify authoritative jurisdiction/date, contract category and exceptions before teaching a legal rule.

rows.objective: Identify floor openings and machine loads as engineered demolition-plan hazards.
rows.remaining: General support/scope lessons are related but do not authorize making disposal openings or placing machinery on floors. Require a competent structural/demolition plan.

rows.objective: Distinguish top-down, underground removal and alternative structural demolition methods without prescribing one universal sequence.
rows.remaining: The source example is not a safe generic execution sequence. Supports, machine placement, retained stability, vibration and jacking alternatives require an approved method.

rows.objective: Separate waste transport, ground/buried-object condition and site clearance from simple visible cleanliness.
rows.remaining: Waste separation exists. Buried-remnant checks and handover criteria require the actual work scope and plan.

rows.objective: Relate subsurface collection points, riser/header route and pumping to groundwater lowering.
rows.remaining: Component roles are taught. Installation order, wash-in operations, pump adjustment and ground movement control are not specified by these lessons.

rows.objective: Coordinate roadwork protection, passing traffic, machinery and workers.
rows.remaining: General interaction is taught; temporary traffic layout, permissions and work boundaries must be checked for the particular site.

rows.objective: Distinguish subgrade, subbase/base and wearing surface without copying one excavation depth or layer arrangement.
rows.remaining: The active lesson already limits depths/materials/layers to the design; no source example becomes a universal specification.

rows.objective: Separate mixture placement with a finisher from compaction with rollers.
rows.remaining: Role distinction exists; distinct roller types, mixture temperature, passes and acceptance criteria remain equipment/material/design-specific.

rows.objective: Separate earthmoving purposes from control-lever/track orientation and transport operations.
rows.remaining: The general machine purposes are taught. Do not supply lever operation or loading/transport instructions without the exact model, qualifications and site plan.

rows.objective: Relate the intended landscape, species, growth and pruning season to the design/client objective.
rows.remaining: General landscape/plants are taught, but seasonal pruning and its differing growth objectives require verified horticultural teaching.

rows.objective: Distinguish ladder/tree work, branch failure and chainsaw/machinery hazards.
rows.remaining: Generic ladder teaching is not a tree-work plan. Do not turn a source height statement into one universal harness or work-at-height rule.

rows.objective: Read fatal-accident counts as historical tables with year, population and classification limits.
rows.remaining: Existing canonical explanation deliberately does not present2020/2021values as current2026rates. Table cells/figure transcription not certified by contact-sheet inspection.

rows.objective: Distinguish falls to a lower level, same-level falls, collisions, falling objects and collapse mechanisms.
rows.remaining: Core distinctions are explicitly taught. Historical ranking is not a complete site risk assessment; detailed figure/table recognition remains unapproved.
